scripts.//typecheck:apps: apps/landing only. apps/storybook is typechecked by its build (yarn storybook:build), NOT by vue-tsc: its tsconfig targets the Vite builder, so a standalone vue-tsc reports 1,671 environment errors -- 699 of them TS5097 against the repo's own mandated .ts import extensions (CLAUDE.md rule 5) and 341 TS2307 for bundler-only modules. See docs/storybook-decisions.md.
scripts.typecheck:all: tsc --noEmit -p packages/tokens/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/contracts/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/testing/tsconfig.json && vue-tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.json && vue-tsc --noEmit -p packages/compat/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/codemods/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/mcp/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p packages/mcp/tsconfig.test.json && yarn typecheck:apps
scripts.//typecheck:all:mcp: TASK-N2-A1. packages/mcp/tsconfig.json EXCLUDES specs, fixtures and scripts because that project EMITS the published dist/. Without tsconfig.test.json in this chain, not one line of the package's tests or its generator was ever typechecked.
scripts.//lint: packages/ AND both apps (TASK-FREE2-01). --max-warnings 0: the baseline is zero errors and zero warnings, so a new warning fails CI rather than accreting into a 'known baseline' everyone ignores. Generated output is excluded via eslint.config.js `ignores`, not CLI globs.
scripts.build: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/contracts build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/testing build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/core build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/compat build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/codemods build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/nuxt build && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/mcp build
scripts.//generate:tokens:dtcg: TASK-N2-T1. Emits packages/tokens/dist/tokens.dtcg.json -- the DTCG 2025.10 interchange projection of the same token maps `tokens:generate` turns into tokens.css. Deliberately NOT folded into `tokens:generate`: that script also rewrites the repo-root DESIGN.md and runs inside `yarn test:prepare`, and the DTCG export must not become a side effect of running the tests. Output is deterministic and timestamp-free -- run it twice and diff. `yarn validate:tokens:dtcg` proves the file on disk is fresh AND that every token in it resolves to the value tokens.css ships.
scripts.//generate:ownership: TASK-OSS-P0-01. Regenerates packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json -- the single deterministic answer to "who owns DzFoo?" that the resolver, the Nuxt module, and the cross-tier ownership map consume. It REPORTS: symbols no authority can classify are emitted as `unclassified` with their evidence, never guessed from a Dz prefix. Core has one tier, so :core is an alias kept for symmetry with Pro.
scripts.//generate:ownership:map: TASK-OSS-P0-02. Merges a Core and a Pro ownership manifest into one exact-name lookup. The Pro input is a FILE produced by a Pro checkout (Pro TASK-GOV-01) -- Core never reads Pro source. Exits non-zero on any cross-tier name collision: a collision is resolved only by a checked-in decision in packages/tooling/src/ownership/collision-decisions.json that names an ADR. Example: yarn generate:ownership:map -- --core packages/core/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --pro ../dzup-ui-pro/packages/pro/manifests/component-ownership.manifest.json --out /tmp/ownership-map.json
scripts.//generate:readme-facts: TASK-OSS-P2-02. Rewrites the marked fact regions of README.md from package.json and the ownership manifest. The package table was hand-typed and five of its six rows named a version the package had already moved past, while two publishable packages were missing entirely. Complements apps/landing build-counts.ts, which owns the separate claims:generated region of the same file.
scripts.//generate:mcp-surface: TASK-N2-A1. Rewrites packages/mcp/docs/mcp-tool-surface.json and the generated tool table in packages/mcp/README.md from a REAL MCP tools/list round-trip against the server the package ships, plus an observed data-source probe per tool (each tool is called through a reader that records the site paths it requests). The tool list previously existed in four hand-typed copies -- the source, the README, the smoke script and the CHANGELOG -- and nothing compared them. Deterministic: it probes committed fixtures, never apps/storybook/public/llms.txt, which is a git-ignored build output.
scripts.//generate:component-meta: TASK-N2-A2. The ONE extraction pipeline. Runs vue-component-meta over every component the ownership manifest classifies public-component or compound-part (208), reading the real .vue/.types.ts through a real TypeScript program, and joins the result to the capability matrix (family/tier/anatomy/evidence state) and to the stories files (verbatim example source) into packages/core/docs/component-meta.json. The docs site (N2-D1), llms-full.txt (N2-A3) and the three metadata MCP tools all read that file; none of them parses a .vue on its own. Drives its component list from the OWNERSHIP manifest, not public-api.manifest.json, which TASK-N2-A1 measured stale by 43 symbols. Deterministic: sorted throughout, printed with LF, absolute paths normalised; two cold runs are byte-identical.
scripts.//generate:llms: TASK-N2-A3. Renders packages/core/docs/llms.txt and llms-full.txt -- the files coding agents read, and the files @dzup-ui/mcp's list_components / get_component answer from -- entirely from packages/core/docs/component-meta.json plus the curated intro prose in packages/tooling/src/llms/llms-content.ts. It replaces apps/storybook/scripts/build-llms.mjs, which was a 567-line SECOND component-API extractor driven by public-api.manifest.json (stale by 43 public components, TASK-N2-A1 finding F1), so those 43 were invisible to every MCP client. apps/storybook's build:llms now only copies the committed output into the served public/ dir. Pure projection: no filesystem walk, no TypeScript program, no .vue parsed.
scripts.//generate:docs-pages: TASK-N2-D1. Writes apps/docs/components/<Name>.md (one per public component), apps/docs/components/index.md and apps/docs/.vitepress/generated/nav.json from packages/core/docs/component-meta.json. The page body is renderComponentSection() -- the SAME function llms-full.txt is rendered by, called with a page-level heading -- so the docs site and the agent documents cannot say different things and there is no second extractor (constraint B9). BEFORE writing anything it re-extracts every component from source and fails if the committed artifact disagrees, reusing validate:component-meta's own freshness clause: apps/docs's build script is `yarn generate && vitepress build`, so a stale artifact turns the SITE build red. Compound parts get no page of their own; all 64 are rendered inside their parent's page. --skip-freshness is a local-loop escape hatch that prints a banner and is refused by --check. TASK-N2-D2 added the evidence layer: an Accessibility-and-evidence section on every component page and six generated pages under apps/docs/evidence/, rendered from quality-matrix.json, capability-matrix.json, e2e/at-matrix/index.json, wcag-deviations.json and the two optional lane records (engine-ratchets.json, security-deviations.json), whose ABSENCE is printed on the page rather than routed around. Three further gates run BEFORE anything is written and refuse rather than report: the at-manual tripwire (a summary cell may not claim more than the append-only AT run records support -- N1-O4 section 6.2 measured that a component whose every pair FAILED resolves to pass, because CellState has no fail value), the capability cross-check (component-meta.json's capability join must agree with the capability matrix it was joined from) and the SC 2.5.7 audit binding (wcag-deviations.json must cover exactly the components the generated drags trait names).
scripts.//validate:hardcoded-strings: TASK-OSS-P4-03. Fails on a user-visible string a component hard-codes: a static aria-label in a template (nobody can change it -- there were 54), or a literal default on a *Text/*Label/*Placeholder prop (only changeable one instance at a time -- there were 39). Reads the <template> block only, so JSDoc @example strings are not swept up. Mark a line `hardcoded-string-ok: <reason>` when the value genuinely is not language; the reason lives at the string, not in a list.
scripts.//validate:tv-slots: TASK-N2-S1, closes N1-O3 finding G1. A tv({ slots }) recipe returns FUNCTIONS; binding one without calling it (`:class="styles.closeButton"`) is valid TypeScript, valid Vue, and renders the element with NO classes at all -- Vue's normalizeClass has no branch for a function. DzLightbox shipped TEN of them and typecheck, lint, unit specs, contract specs and story-DoD all passed. This resolves every slot-bearing recipe in scope for each SFC (sibling and relatively-imported *.variants.ts, plus inline tv()), finds the identifiers they are bound to, and fails on any `binder.slot` / `binder.value.slot` not followed by a call, plus any destructured slot function used as a class value. A slot genuinely wanted as a value says `tv-slot-ok: <reason>` on the line.
scripts.//validate:anatomy-parts: TASK-N2-S1, ADR-19 validation-hook table row 2. Source-level alignment between the `data-part` attributes components EMIT and the anatomies that DECLARE them -- the hook ADR-19 assigns to `validate:contract-parity` and which was never built there, so until now nothing in the repository could see an emitted part with no governing declaration. Every static `data-part="x"` in packages/core/src must be declared by the component's own Dz{Name}.anatomy.ts or by the anatomy of a component that composes it (a compound part such as DzTableRow is covered by DzTable's declaration); every declared non-optional part must be emitted by some source. Reports part names outside the ADR-19 shared vocabulary rather than failing on them, which is what lets the vocabulary grow deliberately.
scripts.//generate:rtl-matrix: TASK-OSS-P4-05. Rewrites packages/core/docs/rtl-matrix.md from the `rtl` field each component declares in its anatomy, so the table cannot drift from the declarations the way a hand-maintained one does.
scripts.//validate:rtl: TASK-OSS-P4-05. A component that declares `rtl: { mirrors: 'layout' }` must not use physical left/right utilities in its variants -- and the generated matrix must match the declarations. A deliberate physical case says `rtl-physical-ok` in the file with its reason (code blocks, `align="left"`, a sheet side the author named). Source-level only: whether `margin-inline-start` resolves to the correct physical edge needs an engine that does layout, which is `expectRtlComputed` in the Playwright lane.
scripts.//generate:form-readiness: TASK-FORM-OSS-01. Rewrites docs/program-2026-08/form-controls-readiness-matrix.md from the ownership manifest (which controls exist), a source probe (what they do), the quality matrix (their APG pattern) and the reviewed assessments in packages/tooling/src/forms/assessments.ts. Nothing in the table is typed by hand, so TASK-FORM-OSS-02 flips a cell by fixing the component and re-running this -- not by editing the row.
scripts.//validate:form-readiness: TASK-FORM-OSS-01. Fails when the committed readiness matrix is stale, when a form control has no assessment or an assessment names a control that no longer exists, and when a reviewed pass carries no evidence. Where a clause is decidable from source -- C2 identity, C3 states, C5 SSR, C6, C7, C8 -- the probe is final and a review cannot upgrade it.
scripts.//generate:quality-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-01. Joins the ownership manifest, the tier rules in @dzup-ui/contracts, and the reviewed assignment in packages/tooling/src/quality/component-tiers.ts into packages/core/docs/quality-matrix.json -- the single answer to "what evidence does DzX owe", which every other P5 packet reads instead of re-deriving it.
scripts.//validate:quality-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-01. The tier assignment is the one handwritten inventory here, so it is the one most able to drift: this fails when a public component has no tier, when a tier is assigned to a symbol that stopped being public, when a Tier C/D or `custom` pattern carries no reason, when a WCAG id or an exception names something outside the catalog, when a component renders teleported content without declaring the trait, when a component's own anatomy contradicts the assignment, or when the generated matrix is stale.
scripts.//generate:matrix-targets: TASK-OSS-P5-03. Rewrites e2e/matrix/targets.generated.ts from quality-matrix.json and the story corpus, so the browser matrix covers every Tier B-D component the moment it becomes public. A component with no story is emitted with `story: null` and reported as unrun, never dropped.
scripts.//generate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Writes one e2e/at-matrix/{Component}.md per Tier B-D component and the index.json the capability matrix reads. The generator owns everything ABOVE the results marker and never rewrites a recorded run below it.
scripts.//validate:at-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-04. Fails on a malformed or unevidenced row -- an unknown AT pair, an unrecognised result, a `pass` with no versions/tester/date/commit behind it, or an index that disagrees with the markdown. Unrun and stale cells are REPORTED, not failed: every row in a new matrix starts unrun, and a gate that failed on that would be switched off the day it landed.
scripts.//generate:at-scripts: TASK-N1-O4. Writes e2e/at-matrix/scripts/{Component}.at-script.md for the 22 Tier C/D components -- the story to open, the keys to press and the announcement the AT must produce, one step per scaffold task. It writes instructions only: no result is read or written here, and nothing under the scaffold's append-only marker is touched.
scripts.//validate:at-scripts: TASK-N1-O4. Script QA, not a test result. Fails when a Tier C/D component has no script, when a scaffold task has no step (or two), when a step invents a task the pattern does not imply, when a step sends a tester to a story id the built Storybook does not have, or when the files on disk have drifted from the data. NOT wired into validate:all -- see the N1-O4 handoff, it is an owner decision.
scripts.//generate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06. Joins the quality matrix, the ownership manifest, the Story DoD report, the AT index, the perf baselines and the browser-matrix ledger into packages/core/docs/capability-matrix.json, plus the narrowed projection the Storybook page imports. One row per public component, one cell per evidence row it owes, marked pass/present/stale/unrun/excepted.
scripts.//validate:capability-matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-06. Fails when the committed matrix is stale, and when a Tier D component carries an `unrun` cell with no artifact behind it -- a Tier D gap is a security gap and does not get to be an empty cell. Stale cells and absent inputs are reported by name, never folded into a count.
scripts.//validate:visual-baselines: TASK-N1-O6. The authority gate for visual baselines. Every committed baseline PNG must have an entry in e2e/visual/visual-baselines.json carrying its SHA-256, the commit it was captured at, who accepted it and why. Fails on a changed digest with no recorded cause, an unaccepted (orphan) image, a recorded image that is gone, an entry with no reason/author, and a covered component missing a theme. Staleness and a gating platform that is not CI's are REPORTED. No browser: Playwright can compare a render to a baseline, it cannot tell a reviewed baseline from an overwritten one.
scripts.//validate:story-dod-tiers: TASK-OSS-P5-02. The triaged half of validate:story-dod: it joins the 366 advisory items to the risk tiers and holds a per-check CEILING on the ones a tier actually requires. The ceiling only falls. A ceiling rather than zero because promoting the checks outright would land 51 red items on a green build, which this packet's own stop condition forbids. `--all` lists the open items; `--write` lowers the ceiling after a fix.
scripts.//perf:capture: TASK-OSS-P5-05. Re-measures every performance baseline: the runtime benchmarks over >= 5 separate processes (cross-process variance is where the two recorded flakes come from) and a tree-shaken fixture build per Tier C/D export. Writes packages/core/perf/baselines.json with the distribution AND the threshold it earned -- or `not yet measurable` when the spread swamps the signal. An owner action, never automatic: a suite that wrote its own baseline every run would ratchet upward forever and call it a budget.
scripts.//validate:tokens:dtcg: TASK-N2-T1. The round-trip gate for the DTCG export: an independent DTCG reader resolves every alias and asserts each resolved value equals what dist/tokens.css computes for the same --dz-* name, in BOTH theme cascades. A name on one side and not the other fails by name. It also re-derives every ABI name from its group path (so a renamed group cannot silently rename a custom property), asserts semantic->primitive references stayed aliases instead of being inlined, checks the export's themeVarying flags against the real cascades, and holds an exact-set ceiling on cross-tier shadowing. Runs with or without a built dist/: CI runs validate:all on a clean checkout before `yarn build`, so when dist/ is absent the declaration blocks are reconstructed from the token maps and the run says so rather than passing vacuously.
scripts.//validate:mcp: TASK-N2-A1. Governs @dzup-ui/mcp the way a public component is governed. Fails when the generated tool surface is stale, when the version differs across package.json / server.json (x2) / CHANGELOG.md / what the server reports over MCP, when server.json's registry entry names another package or advertises an env-var default the source does not use, when a tool has no unit spec, no [malformed] case or no observed data source, or when a ratchet moves the wrong way. It does NOT import the package: packages/tooling is declared with no @dzup-ui/* dependencies, so freshness is delegated to the package's own generator in --check mode and every other clause is an independent read.
scripts.//validate:component-meta: TASK-N2-A2. The freshness gate for packages/core/docs/component-meta.json: re-extracts every component from source and fails on any byte of disagreement (sourceCommit excluded -- it is provenance, and gating on it would fail on every unrelated commit). Also fails when a public component has no record, when a description and its descriptionSource disagree, when an example carries an empty source slice, when one of the nine extraction-debt ratchets moves in either direction, and when apps/landing/scripts/build-registry.ts stops copying the artifact into /r/ -- which is the site path @dzup-ui/mcp reads in production.
scripts.//validate:llms: TASK-N2-A3. The freshness gate for the four agent-facing markdown documents: packages/core/docs/llms{,-full}.txt (the component API) and apps/landing/public/llms{,-full}.txt (the ready-made blocks catalog -- a DIFFERENT document, deliberately, and cross-linked both ways). Fails when a committed file disagrees with a fresh render, when a fence is unbalanced or a GFM table ragged (absorbed from the orphaned apps/storybook/scripts/validate-llms.mjs, now covering four files instead of two), when a public component is not discoverable through the index and the full document by @dzup-ui/mcp's own parsing rules, when apps/storybook/scripts/build-llms.mjs stops copying the generated files into the served public/ dir, when that script starts parsing component sources again (constraint B9), when the curated intro prose states a catalog count, or when a ratchet moves in either direction. Blocks freshness is delegated to apps/landing/scripts/build-registry.ts --check-llms, which loads the catalog through Vite and compares WITHOUT writing -- packages/tooling may not depend on @dzup-ui/*. Pass --no-blocks to skip that ~20 s load.
scripts.//validate:docs-pages: TASK-N2-D1. Fails when a committed docs page disagrees with a fresh render of packages/core/docs/component-meta.json, when a public component has no page, and when a page exists that no public component produces (an orphan left by a rename). Same 'committed output vs regenerated output' shape as validate:readme-facts / validate:llms / validate:component-meta -- the generated pages are committed precisely so this comparison has something to compare against, which is TASK-N2-A3's finding F-4 applied in advance. TASK-N2-D2 widened it to apps/docs/evidence/ -- the same staleness and orphan clauses -- and added the three evidence gates described under //generate:docs-pages, so a stale or overstating evidence artifact fails here as well as in the site build.
scripts.//validate:playground-parity: TASK-N2-D3. The @vue/repl sandbox contract is stated ONCE, in packages/tooling/src/playground/playground-contract.ts: the three asset filenames the bundle producer writes, the bare specifier the sandbox import map binds, and the Tailwind browser-JIT URL without which every tv()-styled component renders unstyled. Three files restate part of it -- apps/storybook/stories/_blocks/playground.config.ts, apps/storybook/scripts/build-playground.mjs and apps/docs/scripts/sync-playground-assets.mjs -- and a drift between them is invisible to every other gate. It is not hypothetical: a third asset name (dzup-core.css) once sat in the Storybook sandbox head for a stylesheet nobody wrote, and every sandbox load 404d.
scripts.//validate:package-names: TASK-OSS-P1-01. Fails when a retired package name reappears outside the paths allowed to record history. Config is data: packages/tooling/scripts/retired-package-names.json. A file that must name a retired package -- a migration note, a test asserting it is never emitted -- says so with a `retired-name-ok: <reason>` comment on the line or the line above.
scripts.//validate:doc-snippets: TASK-OSS-P1-04. Every install snippet marked with a fixture comment must equal the fixture file a test actually builds. Documentation nothing executes drifts, and this repo has paid that bill twice: the docs advertised includePro against a package that never existed, and the module loaded a stylesheet path the tokens package does not export.
scripts.//validate:engines: TASK-OSS-P2-01 / ADR-18. The declared Node floor must (a) be the same number in package.json, .nvmrc and every CI workflow, and (b) be satisfiable by the dependencies the mandatory gates load. It was neither: engines said >=20.0.0 while vite@7 and jsdom@29 require ^20.19.0, and every CI job requested a floating major that resolves to the newest 20.x -- so the floor was a claim nothing ran on.
scripts.//validate:adr-references: TASK-OSS-P3-01, ADR-19. Every ADR-NN cited in source or prose must resolve to a document in docs/adr/ or to an entry in packages/tooling/scripts/adr-registry.json -- a ratcheted debt ledger of the 14 decisions this repository cites but has never written down. The set may only shrink. Put `adr-example-ok:` on a line to exempt an id that is an example rather than a citation.
scripts.validate:all: yarn typecheck && yarn lint && yarn validate:boundaries && yarn validate:interaction-contract && yarn validate:contract-parity && yarn validate:hardcoded-strings && yarn validate:tv-slots && yarn validate:anatomy-parts && yarn validate:rtl && yarn validate:form-readiness && yarn validate:quality-tiers && yarn validate:story-status && yarn validate:story-dod && yarn validate:story-dod-tiers && yarn validate:at-matrix && yarn validate:capability-matrix && yarn validate:visual-baselines && yarn validate:tokens && yarn validate:tokens:dtcg && yarn validate:exports && yarn validate:ownership && yarn validate:mcp && yarn validate:component-meta && yarn validate:llms && yarn validate:docs-pages && yarn validate:playground-parity && yarn validate:package-names && yarn validate:doc-snippets && yarn validate:engines && yarn validate:adr-references && yarn validate:readme-facts && yarn validate:externals && yarn validate:dts && yarn validate:changelog && yarn validate:peers && yarn validate:licenses
scripts.//test:nuxt-fixtures: TASK-OSS-P1-03. Real Nuxt consumer apps, installed from packed tarballs and staged OUTSIDE this repository -- a fixture kept inside the monorepo resolves the repo's own nuxt/nitropack/vite through Node's upward directory walk and stops being a consumer test. Three steps because one install is ~800 packages and one build is ~60s: :pack (yarn pack + stage), :install (npm install each), then the assertions. Set DZUP_PRO_TARBALL to a tarball produced by a Pro checkout to include the core-pro fixture; without it that fixture reports `unrun`, not `skipped`.
scripts.test:e2e:functional: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/a11y e2e/components e2e/smoke
scripts.//test:e2e:matrix: TASK-OSS-P5-03. The three-engine x five-condition lane over every Tier B-D component: chromium/firefox/webkit x {default, forced-colors, reduced-motion, rtl, touch, zoom-400}. Results are per cell, not an aggregate pass count -- set PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT to emit the report the capability matrix reads. Tier A stays in the single chromium lane e2e/components already gives it. Pass --project=matrix-webkit-rtl (or --shard) to run one cell.
scripts.test:e2e:matrix: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/matrix
scripts.//test:e2e:matrix:prebuilt: The same lane against an ALREADY-built apps/storybook/storybook-static. Separate because one Storybook build is ~4 minutes and the lane is normally re-run many times against one build.
scripts.test:e2e:visual: yarn workspace @dzup-ui/tokens build && DZUP_GALLERY=1 yarn storybook:build && STORYBOOK_E2E_STATIC=1 STORYBOOK_E2E_PREBUILT=1 playwright test e2e/visual --max-failures=1
scripts.//test:e2e:visual:pilot: TASK-N1-O6. The per-component visual lane over the families e2e/visual/visual-baselines.json opts in (pilot: buttons), light and dark, chromium, LTR. Needs a built apps/storybook/storybook-static; it does NOT need DZUP_GALLERY=1, because it drives the same component stories the browser matrix drives rather than the demo screens. Baselines change only through `yarn visual:accept`.
scripts.//visual:accept: TASK-N1-O6. Accept exactly ONE visual baseline, with --by and --reason both required: `yarn visual:accept --component DzButton --theme dark --by "<name>" --reason "<what changed and why the new image is correct>"`. One snapshot per invocation is the constraint that replaces the perf lane's downward ratchet -- a different image is not `worse`, so the cost of accepting scales with how much changed instead. --record-only re-digests an image already on disk; --bootstrap records baselines that have no entry yet and can never re-accept a changed one.
scripts.//test:e2e:update: TASK-N1-O6. REMOVED. It was `playwright test --update-snapshots` -- one command that rewrote every committed baseline in the repository in a single anonymous act. Kept as a signpost so nobody re-derives the flag from the Playwright docs; it prints the accept workflow and exits 1.
scripts.//test:e2e:landing: TASK-FREE3-06. The landing's own Playwright suite (apps/landing/e2e): the five core flows, the pixel/blank-page guards, the hero baselines, and a Pixel 7 project. `:preview` swaps the dev server for `vite preview` over apps/landing/dist -- that is what CI runs, so the browser drives the artifact users actually receive. Both scripts invoke @playwright/test's own CLI rather than the `playwright` bin shim; see the note in apps/landing/playwright.config.ts.
scripts.//test:responsive:landing: The block responsive-certification sweep: every block at each breakpoint in both text directions. Kept as its own script because it is the one spec worth running alone against a single block change; the full `test:e2e:landing` run includes it. `:ci` pins workers and fails the run on a flaky pass rather than letting a retry launder it.
scripts.//docs: TASK-N2-D1. The public documentation site (apps/docs, VitePress). `docs` regenerates the component pages then starts the dev server; `docs:build` is the local static build; `docs:preview` serves apps/docs/.vitepress/dist. NOT deployed or hosted by any task -- see README §3 <authority>.
scripts.storybook:install: yarn install && yarn workspace @dzup-ui/storybook exec playwright install chromium
